claim_text: Claude Fable 5's individual requests on hard tasks can run for many minutes and autonomous runs for hours, which is one of the largest shifts teams encounter on migration: client timeouts, streaming, and progress indicators need adjusting, and harnesses are better restructured to check on runs asynchronously than to block
evidence_span: This is one of the largest shifts teams encounter when adjusting to Claude Fable 5. Adjust client timeouts, streaming, and user-facing progress indicators before migrating, and consider restructuring harnesses to check on runs asynchronously, for example through scheduled jobs, rather than blocking.

claim_text: On Claude Fable 5 effort is the primary control for the intelligence, latency, and cost trade-off: high is the default for most tasks, xhigh for the most capability-sensitive workloads, medium or low for routine work — and its lower effort settings often exceed xhigh performance on prior models
evidence_span: Use `high` as the default for most tasks, with `xhigh` for the most capability-sensitive workloads and `medium` or `low` for routine work. Lower effort settings on Claude Fable 5 still perform well and often exceed `xhigh` performance on prior models.

claim_text: Claude Fable 5's instruction-following is improved enough that a brief instruction steers most behaviors, so enumerating each behavior by name is unnecessary
evidence_span: Instruction-following is improved enough that you can steer most behaviors with a brief instruction rather than enumerating each behavior by name.

claim_text: Instructing Claude Fable 5 to audit each progress claim against an actual tool result nearly eliminated fabricated status reports in Anthropic's testing, even on tasks designed to elicit them
evidence_span: In Anthropic's testing, this nearly eliminated fabricated status reports even on tasks designed to elicit them

claim_text: Separate, fresh-context verifier subagents tend to outperform self-critique, so long-running prompts should make self-verification explicit by scheduling subagent checks against the specification at an interval
evidence_span: Separate, fresh-context verifier subagents tend to outperform self-critique.

claim_text: Skills developed for prior models are often too prescriptive for Claude Fable 5 and can degrade its output quality, so migration means reviewing and removing older instructions wherever default performance is better
evidence_span: Skills developed for prior models are often too prescriptive for Claude Fable 5 and can degrade output quality. Review and consider removing older instructions if default performance is better.

claim_text: Showing Claude Fable 5 a remaining-token countdown is what most often triggers it to suggest a new session, offer to summarize and hand off, or trim its own work, so harnesses should avoid surfacing explicit context-budget counts
evidence_span: In very long sessions, Claude Fable 5 can occasionally suggest a new session, offer to summarize and hand off, or trim its own work. This is most often triggered when the harness shows a remaining-token countdown to the model.
